title: I made rover races on Mars, the Moon and Europa. Where do they fall short, and what should I add next?
author: Loud-Current1641
selftext:
Play (free, browser, phones OK): [https://junzzy827.github.io/solar-odyssey/?lang=en](https://junzzy827.github.io/solar-odyssey/?lang=en)



Three rover races, each built around what makes that world different:



Mars: a 16-gate zigzag course on the floor of Valles Marineris, from real HiRISE height data. Rocks trip your wheels, so you jump them.

Moon: a chase at the Apollo 17 landing valley. 1/6 gravity, huge jumps, side thrusters in the air. On the way you can drive past the real Apollo 17 sites (the lander, the flag, the geology stations) at their surveyed positions.

Europa: an ice drift race in the trough of an ice ridge. Steer too hard and you spin.

Every run leaves a ghost, and the #1 time races you in gold, thanks to u/cratercamper, who built the ghost and hiscore system.



Where I know it falls short (help wanted):



The ground doesn't look real enough yet. The heights come from real data, but up close Mars can still read like a sandy desert on Earth, and the Moon and Europa surfaces look too smooth and even. What makes a planetary surface look real to you? Rock size and spread, dust, colour variation, lighting, the way the horizon falls away?

The rover isn't very detailed. It's a simple model with basic suspension. Compared with real rovers it lacks the small parts (cables, sensors, wheel treads, dust on the body), and it doesn't feel heavy. Any tips on what details matter most at game-camera distance, or how to make the driving feel weightier?

And ideas for what comes next:



Another world? (Titan's dunes in thick haze, Io next to lava lakes, a comet with almost no gravity, Mercury at sunrise...)

A new kind of race? (relay, time attack at night, collect samples on the way, a race against an incoming dust storm...)

Anything that would make the existing races more fun?

Screenshots of real rover photos, references, or wild ideas are all welcome. My kid and I read every comment.

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Loud-Current1641 could you please add details on how AI was used to make this? Rule 4 is there to make sure promotional posts contribute by getting into the process and actual development. There's a real risk of the sub being swamped by self-promotion with nothing to discuss otherwise. If you don't update, this post may be removed.
